note: Original description, with the alate, queen, soldier and worker all present. The genus was Eutermes originally and is now Nasutitermes. The original was OCR'd from a library scan at the Internet Archive.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: (Placed in Eutermes in the original.) General colour ochre, head dark chestnut, compound eyes black, wings dark brown, the thoracic nota, an oval spot on each side of the meso- and metathorax, and the chitinous plates of the abdomen dark brown. Head circular and densely hairy, the top flat and dark brown, only the base of the postclypeus, the ocelli and the labial palps ochre; frons broadly concave in front; base of the postclypeus truncate in front and divided by a darker median suture, the anteclypeus white, slightly projecting in the middle and with a white median line; labrum large and rounded in front; mandibles broad and triangular, the left mandible with a very sharp apical tooth, below it a blunter tooth, then a rounded sharp part connected to a third blunt tooth, and a large blunt tooth at the basal angle, the right mandible with two blunt horn-like teeth and a darker, finely toothed basal area; compound eyes large and circular; ocelli large, oval and oblique, at some distance from the inner margin of the compound eyes; fontanelle appearing as a narrow white line in the middle of the frons; antennae 14-segmented, long and slender, dark chestnut-brown, paler at the tip and the base, segment 1 very long and stout, segment 2 much smaller, segment 3 slightly longer and narrower than segment 2, from segment 4 onwards longer than wide, rounded at the sides and broader at the tip than at the base, segments 13 and 14 the longest, the terminal segment elongate and rounded at the tip; pronotum wider than long and narrower than the head, the margins dark chestnut, truncate in front with a paler median line, densely long-haired, the anterior angles broadly rounded and sloping steeply backwards, the posterior margin deeply concave in the middle; meso- and metathorax pale brown with a paler median line; legs normal, femora and tibiae about equal in length, tarsi short; wings greyish brown, the two costal veins strong and reaching the broadly rounded tip, the wing more than 3 times as long as wide (almost 4 times), the media running slightly above the middle of the wing and forked at the tip, sometimes giving off an unbranched straight vein to the margin, the cubitus giving off 4—5 very thick oblique veins and 7—8 paler ones; abdomen long and rounded, densely hairy; cerci thick and dark. Measurements: body length with wings 14 mm, body length without wings 7.5 mm, head length 1.37 mm, head width 1.18 mm, pronotum length 0.59 mm, width 0.89 mm, fore wing length 11 mm, width 3 mm, hind wing length 11.5 mm, width 3.5 mm, abdominal width 2 mm.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Similar to the soldier of E. fumipennis Walker, but the head smaller and the sides more distinctly narrowing towards the nasus, much paler (pale brown), with a large area in the middle of the occiput and the region around the antennal fossae even paler; the lateral outline of the head quite different; antennae always 12-segmented, segment 1 stouter but narrower than in E. fumipennis, segment 2 much smaller and about one third of the length of segment 1, segment 3 longer than segment 2 and distinctly broader at the tip than at the base, segment 4 slightly shorter than segment 3 and longer than wide, the sides far more rounded than in E. fumipennis; segments 5—11 gradually longer and more slender, paler at the tip and the base, segment 12 slightly longer and more slender than in E. fumipennis; labial palps long and slender, pale brown; pronotum very small, the anterior margin raised into a dark ridge; legs longer and more slender than in E. fumipennis, white-yellow; abdomen slender and rounded; cerci thick. Measurements: body length 3.5 mm, head length 1.46 mm (including the nasus), nasus length 0.93 mm, nasus base width 0.17 mm, head width 0.82 mm, pronotum length 0.27 mm, width 0.48 mm, abdominal width 0.91 mm.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: White, head pale brown, covered above by a large darker red-brown or pale yellow patch divided by a pale white-yellow median band which joins a pale transverse band in front, with a distinct dark chitinous dot on either side in front of the antennae and a short white line on either side of the median band on the occiput; base of the postclypeus rounded and convex, the base of the anteclypeus concave, rounded at the sides and narrowing towards the rounded tip; labrum large, broad and convex, rounded at the tip; mandibles triangular, the left mandible with two sharp apical teeth, below them a very small blunt tooth and a black projecting basal-angle tooth, the right mandible with two less sharp apical teeth and a broad black finely toothed basal angle; antennae 13-segmented, pale yellow, segment 1 rather slender, segment 2 only half as long, segment 3 the shortest, the next 5 segments wider than long, segments 9—12 longer than wide, segment 13 more slender and rounded at the tip; pronotum narrow, the anterior part raised into a ridge, saddle-shaped; legs rather short; abdomen rounded, the tergites pale yellow. Measurements: body length 4 mm, head length 1.2 mm, head width 0.95 mm, pronotum length 0.29 mm, width 0.59 mm, abdominal width 1.18 mm.

sections.label: Other
sections.text: Close to E. fumipennis but differing in the antennal segment counts: this species has 14 segments in the alate and always 12 and 13 in the soldier and worker, the only known Australian species with this combination (in E. fumigatus the alate, soldier and worker have 15/13/14 segments respectively). Distribution confined to the east of the Australian mainland, a rainforest or scrub species: Blackal Range and Mt. Tambourine in southern Queensland, Herberton, Malanda and Cedar Creek in northern Queensland (alates in the 4th month). The queen is much smaller than that of E. magnus Froggatt, white-yellow, with the head, thoracic segments, legs and 10 chitinous plates of the abdomen darker, the first plate rounded at the sides, the next 7 rectangular, the last 2 smaller and rounded at the sides, the first 4 segments far broader and more swollen than those behind; queen measurements: body length 14.2 mm, head length 1.37 mm, head width 1.18 mm, pronotum length 0.59 mm, width 0.89 mm, abdominal width (at segment 4) 4.6 mm.
